facts.statement: If classified as a rebbachisaurid, Histriasaurus would be one of the oldest known members of that group.
facts.quote: It has been suggested to be a rebbachisaurid, and if so one of the oldest known members of the group

facts.statement: The holotype specimen WN V-6 was found in a bonebed off the coast of Bale, Croatia, by Dario Boscarolli in the 1980s.
facts.quote: The holotype, specimen WN V-6, was found in a bonebed in lacustrine limestone exposed on the seafloor off the coast of the town of Bale on the Istrian peninsula in Croatia by Dario Boscarolli during the 1980s

facts.statement: Histriasaurus was described in 1998 by Dalla Vecchia.
The specific name H. boscarollii honors the discoverer of the fossil site, Darío Boscarolli.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the discoverer of the site, Darío Boscarolli

facts.statement: Some authors consider Histriasaurus a dubious taxon, while others support its original classification.
facts.quote: Although some authors consider Histriasaurus a dubious taxon, more recent papers support the original classification

facts.statement: Histriasaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous, from the Hauterivian to Barremian stages, approximately 135 to 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: Early Cretaceous (Hauterivian to Barremian stages, around 135-125 million years ago)

facts.statement: The time range for Histriasaurus is the Hauterivian to Barremian, from 132.6 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Barremian (132.6 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Histriasaurus coexisted with various indeterminate dinosaurs including a camarasaurid, a titanosauriform, a somphospondylian, and a theropod.
facts.quote: Histriasaurus would have coexisted with an indeterminate camarasaurid, an indeterminate titanosauriform, an indeterminate somphospondylian, an indeterminate theropod, an indeterminate dinosaur of unknown classification and the foraminiferan Campanellula capuensis
